candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9: perform targeted screening assessments; educate adults age 65 and older; assess health risks and home/environmental management needs.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — older-adult driving-safety assessment and counseling
candidate.educational_objective: Evaluate older-driver safety using individualized functional assessment rather than chronological age alone and refer for further driving evaluation when specific concerns are identified.

options.A: Recommend driving cessation solely because of chronological age without first assessing vision, cognition, motor function, or driving-related abilities.
options.B: Assess driving-related vision, cognition, and motor/sensory function and discuss referral for a formal driving evaluation when specific concerns are identified.
options.C: Ignore declining vision or slower reaction time because healthcare professionals have no role in counseling about driving-safety concerns.
options.D: Treat one abnormal office measure as conclusive proof of unsafe driving without considering the broader functional assessment.

candidate.rationale: NHTSA states that decisions about driving ability should never be based on age alone. Its clinician guidance describes assessment of driving-related functional domains including vision, cognition, and motor/sensory function to identify specific concerns and supports referral for additional driving evaluation when indicated. B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Older-driver fitness should be assessed individually rather than determined by age alone; vision, cognition and motor/sensory function are relevant domains, and further driving evaluation may be appropriate when concerns are identified.
candidate.source_document_title: Older Drivers; Licensing Agency Referrals / Clinician’s Guide to Assessing and Counseling Older Drivers
candidate.source_locator: Older Drivers: decisions about ability to drive should never be based on age alone; changes in vision, physical fitness, reflexes/attention can affect safety. Licensing Agency Referrals: CADReS assesses key functional areas of vision, cognition, and motor/sensory functions and helps identify concerns related to driving; clinicians may refer drivers for additional evaluation.
candidate.source_version_date: Current NHTSA older-driver guidance; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
candidate.stem: An older adult has declining vision and slower reaction time and asks whether age alone means driving must stop immediately. Which nursing approach is most appropriate?
